evidence.title: Multicenter Histology Image Integration and Multiscale Deep Learning Support Machine Learning–Enabled Pediatric Sarcoma Classification
evidence.abstract: Pediatric sarcomas present diagnostic challenges due to their rarity and diverse subtypes, often requiring specialized pathology expertise and costly genetic tests. To overcome these barriers, we developed a computational pipeline leveraging deep learning methods to accurately classify pediatric sarcoma subtypes from digitized histology slides. To ensure classifier generalizability and minimize center-specific artifacts, a dataset comprising 867 whole-slide images (WSI) from three medical centers and the Children's Oncology Group was collected and harmonized. Multiple convolutional neural network and vision transformer (ViT) architectures were systematically evaluated as feature extractors for SAMPLER-based WSI representations, and input parameters, such as tile size combinations and resolutions, were tested and optimized. The analysis showed that advanced ViT foundation models (UNI and CONCH) significantly outperformed earlier approaches, and incorporating multiscale features enhanced classification accuracy. The optimized models achieved high performance, distinguishing rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) from non-RMS soft-tissue sarcomas (NRSTS) with an AUC of 0.969 and differentiating RMS subtypes (alveolar vs. embryonal) with an AUC of 0.961. Additionally, a two-stage pipeline effectively identified scarce Ewing sarcoma images from other NRSTS (AUC = 0.929). title: Efficient Machine Learning Framework for Detecting e-Commerce Fraud Transactions
abstract: The fast pace of e-commerce has also come with a high risk of fraudulent activities that require sophisticated detection systems that balances accuracy, efficiency, and flexibility. This analysis describes a machine-learning-based approach to fraudulent online purchases with the aid of the E-commerce Fraud Dataset. The methodology uses the data preprocessing by removing inconsistencies, feature selection, categorical encoding, and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address the class imbalance. Two suggested models, Linear Regression (LiR) and Decision Tree (DT), were applied and tested in comparison to baseline classifier, i.e., Support Vector Machine (SVM) and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The accuracy (Acc), precision (Prec), recall (Rec), F1-score as well as ROC analysis were used to determine performance. The experimental results indicate that LiR performed better with 96% Acc, 96% Prec, 96% Rec, and a 95% F1score whereas DT scored 89% Acc, 89% Prec, 89% Rec, and 89% F1score. Conversely, SVM and KNN had a lower accuracy of 68% and 50.8, respectively, which validates the high effectiveness of the proposed models. LiR model is robust, scalable and efficient to real time applications whereas DT is efficient in the interpretation aspect which is based on a rule-based structure. This study adds a valid and viable pipeline of detection of frauds, enhancing trust and safety in e-commerce structures.

title: Hybrid S-Box and Caesar-Based Polyalphabetic Cipher for Enhanced Lightweight Encryption
abstract: Lightweight cryptography has become essential for securing data in resource constrained platforms such as IoT sensor nodes, RFID tags, and embedded microcontrollers. Classical ciphers like Caesar and Vigenere are computationally efficient but exhibit weak confusion, low entropy, and almost zero avalanche, making them unsuitable for modern security requirements. This paper proposes a hybrid lightweight stream cipher that combines a Caesar-based modular addition with a key-dependent AES S-Box substitution and an ARX-driven keystream generator. The design introduces nonlinear confusion and per-byte diffusion while maintaining a low computational footprint suitable for 8-bit and 16-bit microcontrollers. This work shows that the proposed cipher significantly improves ciphertext randomness, achieving 7.21 bits/byte entropy and improved avalanche effect compared to classical ciphers. Hardware estimations show that the cipher requires approximately 450–550 Gate Equivalents (GEs), which is much lower than AES (3400–5000 GEs) and PRESENT (1570 GEs). These results indicate that the hybrid cipher provides a practical balance between security and computational efficiency, making it suitable for lightweight IoT environments.

title: KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION ALGORITHMS FOR NATURAL HUMAN-MACHINE INTERACTION
abstract: This study examines advanced algorithms for knowledge representation that facilitate natural human-machine interaction in intelligent systems. The research addresses the fundamental challenge of enabling computers to process arbitrary user queries without requiring specialized training from users. Through a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental validation, we propose a framework for knowledge representation that preserves semantic relevance while supporting flexible query processing. The methodology incorporates fractal knowledge structures and production systems that maintain both global and local knowledge properties. Results demonstrate significant improvements in query comprehension and response accuracy compared to traditional knowledge-based systems. The findings have important implications for the development of more intuitive and accessible artificial intelligence systems across various application domains.

title: PitchPal-AI Startup Pitch Deck & Idea Validator
abstract: The startup world which is full of disorder hardly leads to any other problems besides those entrepreneurs face in the areas of structuring, validating, and pitching their business ideas to investors. Apart from being a very lengthy procedure, a pitch deck in the traditional manner also heavily relies on a subjective point of view of a researcher, manual research, and very limited market insights, thus the process becomes inefficient while the results are inconsistent. We, therefore, introduce PitchPal, a revolutionary AI-powered framework for spectacularly automatic idea validation and pitch deck generation leveraging cutting-edge technologies from NLP and Transformer-based models. PitchPal is an ensemble of three essential components: Firstly, an Idea Intelligence Engine, which performs semantic analysis and assesses market relevance. Secondly, a Generative Pitch Deck Creator, which produces uniform storytelling investor-ready slides. At last, but not least, a Validation Scoring System, which scores the innovation potential, market fit, and feasibility of the idea. Through extensive experimental evaluations on a startup ideas dataset comprising over 1,000 instances, PitchPal has shown to significantly enhance the quality of the content, reduce the preparation time, and increase the communication power with investors. As such, this system is a milestone in the journey of AI-powered entrepreneurship support, as it makes startup development and presentation based on data and insights, not only fast, but also accurate.

title: An enhanced parrot optimizer with multiple strategies for wireless sensor network node deployment
abstract: This paper presents an Enhanced parrot Optimizer (EPO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm that synergistically integrates multiple advanced strategies to address the critical limitations of the original parrot Optimizer (PO)-namely, poor initial population diversity, susceptibility to premature convergence, slow convergence speed, and the absence of an effective restart mechanism. EPO introduces five key innovations across its behavioral phases: (1) Cubic chaotic mapping is employed to generate a high-quality, well-distributed initial population, enhancing global exploration from the outset; (2) a risk-aware alert-contraction mechanism-inspired by predator-avoidance strategies in swarm intelligence-is embedded in the staying behavior to proactively detect and escape local optima; (3) a nonlinear decay factor dynamically balances exploration and exploitation during the communicating behavior phase; (4) a dual-layer intelligent judgment system governs the "fear of strangers" behavior, combining elite-guided convergence (outer layer) with diversity preservation (inner layer); and (5) a hybrid local restart mechanism is activated upon three consecutive generations of stagnation, applying t-distribution perturbation to low-fitness individuals for large-scale jumps and Differential Evolution (DE) to high-fitness individuals for refined local search.The performance of EPO is rigorously evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark suite at 30, 50, and 100 dimensions, with comprehensive comparisons against eleven state-of-the-art metaheuristic algorithms-including PO, MPO, SMO, BTO, HOA, HHO, DBO, BKA, PSO, DE, and the Ivy algorithm. EPO achieves the best mean ranking across all dimensionalities (2.31 at 30D, 2.03 at 50D, and 1.83 at 100D), consistently outperforming all competitors in terms of solution accuracy, convergence speed, and stability. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at a significance level of α = 0.05 confirm that the EPO algorithm achieves statistically significantly better performance than its competitors in 212 cases (81.2%) at 30D, 225 cases (86.2%) at 50D, 225 cases (86.2%) at 50D, 239 cases (91.6%) at 100D. Furthermore, EPO is successfully applied to the real-world Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) node deployment problem, consistently outperforming the original PO across different network scales: with 20 nodes, coverage improves from 0.7765 to 0.8284 (+ 6.7%); with 30 nodes, from 0.9285 to 0.9871 (+ 6.3%); and with 40 nodes, from 0.9826 to 0.9992 (+ 1.7%).Collectively, these findings validate that EPO not only advances the theoretical foundation of parrot-inspired optimization but also provides a powerful and reliable tool for solving complex real-world optimization problems.

title: ESQAD: A curriculum-aligned dataset for question answer generation in Spanish
abstract: This paper presents ESQAD (Educational Spanish Question-Answer Dataset), an open-access resource for question-answer generation (QAG) in Spanish aligned with national curricula. ESQAD comprises 6,980 expert-curated exam questions, 340 literary comprehension items, 47 legal FAQs, and 913 LLM-generated pairs validated in academic settings. The dataset covers diverse linguistic and cognitive features, including subject classification, question typologies, and Bloom-level complexity. We analyze lexical diversity, cognitive intent, and structure across subsets. The automatically generated portion was created with Bloom-guided prompts and large language models (LLMs), and evaluated through both computational metrics and classroom validation. Results show that cognitive-level control is reliable for factual recall but only partial for higher-order reasoning. All resources, including dataset, code, and validation tool, are publicly available. ESQAD provides a structured benchmark for curriculum-aware QAG in under-resourced languages, with applications in educational NLP, question generation, and adaptive learning.

title: The Illusion of Cognition: Why Behavioural Imitation Cannot Achieve Genuine Cognition
abstract: Contemporary artificial intelligence systems increasingly exhibit behaviours associated with perception, reasoning, learning, and goal-directed action. These successes have encouraged the assumption that continued scaling of existing architectures may eventually yield genuine cognition. This paper challenges that assumption by treating cognition as an organisational property that requires, but is not reducible to, behavioural success. We define cognition as an organisationally closed system of mutually implicative capacities. Based on a historical reconstruction of the cognitive vocabulary instantiated or attributed to AI systems across paradigms, we derive eight interdependent cognitive capacity groups and formalise their dependency relations. Evaluating contemporary AI systems against this organisational criterion, we show that despite extensive behavioural competence, none instantiate the closure required for cognition. We then explain why this structural absence nevertheless produces a persistent illusion of cognition. Contemporary AI systems are optimised almost exclusively for behavioural imitation: loss functions evaluate output adequacy without constraining internal organisation. Any structure sufficient to reproduce target behaviour is equally acceptable, while organisational features required for cognition—endogenous goals, internal epistemic access, and reciprocal functional integration—are systematically excluded. Scaling reduces behavioural error but leaves these absences intact, thereby intensifying the appearance of cognition without approaching it. Finally, we discuss the implications of this diagnosis. Our analysis suggests a structural bifurcation: continued scaling of behaviourally optimised systems preserves performance while precluding cognition, or pursuing AI architectures that target organisational closure beyond mere behavioural success is necessary to preserve the possibility of AGI.

abstract: Abstract: Source code and manifest files for Nexus AI, a browser-based neural audio synthesis engine. title: Kidney Tumor Detection in CT scans Combining 3D CNN and Transformer Networks
abstract: Timely and precise diagnosis of kidney tumors by CT scans is crucial for optimal patient outcomes and treatment decisions. Volumetric and spatial features in medical images can be effectively detected using conventional approaches such as 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (3D-CNN). They frequently run into problems when trying to capture the big picture and long-range linkages in complex organizations. This research makes use of a novel deep learning strategy that improves kidney tumor detection through the use of a 3D-CNN and a Transformer network. The 3D-CNN part uses data from CT scans to learn about local features and textures, while the Transformer part uses a self-attention method to better grasp broad patterns. This synergy makes the model more robust and precise, which in turn enhances its understanding of both fine-grained details and the overall picture. Results show that combining CNNs with attention-based frameworks improves cancer detection and medical picture analysis, and the innovative approach outperforms conventional CNN models in tests. Because it outperforms previous, less sophisticated models, the "Kidney Tumor Detection in CT scans Combining 3DCNN and Transformer Networks" method has gained a lot of praise. This hybrid method has a higher success rate, according to the study literature you cited, even if the given data file only shows that 18.34% of the total 12,446 records are classified as Tumor (which is based on sample amount, not results). In particular, hybrid models, such as the Hybrid Deep MSFPT Transformer, outperform pure Transformers or standard CNNs (e.g., Faster R-CNN) by a few percentage points when it comes to detection tasks, with performance metrics reaching as high as 97.20% Precision and 97.10% F1-Score. The approach was successful because it played on its two main strengths: Understanding the entire structure and relationship between the tumor and the kidney requires 3DCNNs to quickly extract local, volumetric features that are critical for establishing exact tumor boundaries, and Transformer Networks to capture the global context and long-range dependencies across the CT slices. It is considered "very good" in comparison to other project models because of the synergistic combination that makes it a more dependable and stronger diagnostic tool.

title: Graph neural network solutions for interpretable anomaly detection in IT infrastructure monitoring time series
abstract: Anomaly detection is an essential task for many firms and organizations. Identifying unusual patterns in messy multivariate time series can prevent catastrophic events and optimize operations. Traditional statistical methods struggle with high-dimensional data and complex temporal dependencies. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), a reconstruction-based framework, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for effective and interpretable anomaly detection. Our method involves representing multivariate time series as graphs and training two interconnected GANs and an Autoencoder to capture the normal behaviour of the networks. Anomalies are detected by measuring the reconstruction error and the discriminator’s score. Our case study on the signals of the INFN CNAF Tier-1 data centre demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in terms of robustness and interpretability. We further validate our model on two widely used benchmark datasets for IT infrastructure monitoring, PSM and SMD, obtaining Fβ scores of 0.943 and 0.763, respectively. This work highlights the potential of GNNs in developing interpretable deep learning solutions for real-world applications.

title: Towards a Cryogenic Photonic Ising Machine: Phase-Coupled Silicon-Nitride Resonators for Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: This comprehensive technical paper proposes a novel cryogenic photonic computing architecture for energy-efficient combinatorial optimization. The authors design a 256-spin prototype system based on phase-coupled silicon-nitride (Si₃N₄) micro-ring resonators operating at liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K). Unlike conventional digital approaches, the system encodes spin variables as continuous geometric phases (Φ ∈ [0, 2π]) in ultra-high-Q optical cavities, with spin-spin interactions implemented through evanescent coupling between adjacent resonators. The paper presents detailed device specifications, fabrication protocols, and performance projections comparing photonic Ising machines against existing platforms including digital annealers, quantum computers, and GPU-based solvers. Theoretical analysis predicts intrinsic energy dissipation approaching ~10⁻¹⁸ J per spin update—three orders of magnitude below CMOS—though cooling overhead currently dominates system-level energy consumption. Extensive case studies explore applications across drug discovery (fragment-based design), financial services (portfolio optimization), logistics (vehicle routing), manufacturing (job shop scheduling), healthcare (radiation therapy planning), and smart cities (traffic control). The authors provide honest assessments of both advantages and limitations, including scalability barriers, connectivity constraints, and the critical challenge of cooling overhead that limits practical deployment to continuous-operation scenarios. With comprehensive appendices covering implementation details, benchmark specifications, error analysis, risk assessment, and ethical considerations, this work establishes a foundation for experimental validation while acknowledging the 40-60% probability of achieving modest performance improvements over classical methods. The paper emphasizes this is a proof-of-concept proposal requiring rigorous experimental validation rather than a demonstrated breakthrough.

The paper presents detailed device specifications, fabrication protocols, and performance projections comparing photonic Ising machines against existing platforms including digital annealers, quantum computers, and GPU-based solvers. Theoretical analysis predicts intrinsic energy dissipation approaching ~10⁻¹⁸ J per spin update—three orders of magnitude below CMOS—though cooling overhead currently dominates system-level energy consumption. Extensive case studies explore applications across drug discovery (fragment-based design), financial services (portfolio optimization), logistics (vehicle routing), manufacturing (job shop scheduling), healthcare (radiation therapy planning), and smart cities (traffic control). The authors provide honest assessments of both advantages and limitations, including scalability barriers, connectivity constraints, and the critical challenge of cooling overhead that limits practical deployment to continuous-operation scenarios. With comprehensive appendices covering implementation details, benchmark specifications, error analysis, risk assessment, and ethical considerations, this work establishes a foundation for experimental validation while acknowledging the 40-60% probability of achieving modest performance improvements over classical methods. The paper emphasizes this is a proof-of-concept proposal requiring rigorous experimental validation rather than a demonstrated breakthrough.

title: Drift detection on feature attributions for monitoring visual reinforcement learning models in maritime port surveillance
abstract: Background: Maritime activity is expanding globally, increasing the demand for robust port security systems capable of detecting illegal trafficking. Due to the growing sophistication of smuggling methods, law enforcement agencies require advanced surveillance and prevention technologies such as those developed in the SMAUG project. In this context, initiatives such as the SMAUG project aim to deliver integrated surveillance capabilities coordinated by a high-level deep reinforcement learning (DRL) decision-making system that operates on image-based environmental representations. Despite their effectiveness, DRL models are closed-boxes, complicating continuous model monitoring (CMM). Conventional drift detection captures shifts in input or output distributions yet often fails to explain underlying problems. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques can provide a complementary approach with insights into the agent's inner workings, enabling monitoring of the concept rather than just the data. Methods: We propose FADMON, an XAI-driven concept drift detection method for image-based models. FADMON performs statistical drift tests on feature attributions to detect deviations in learned policies. We demonstrate how FADMON can enhance CMM with a three-stage model monitoring architecture that enables semi-supervised explainable model monitoring. We validate our approach with SMAUG's decision-making DRL model on a simulated maritime port surveillance environment under multiple unforeseen scenarios. Results: FADMON consistently flags drift on all drifted scenarios with mean p-values of 0.000 with no variance trough 30 repetitions, with lower mean p-values (0.553±0.215) on non-drifted scenarios with respect to other established drift detection methodologies such as prior probability shift detection (0.65 ± 0.000), though well above the standard 0.05 threshold. Conclusions: FADMON can add an explainability layer to the monitoring system while also supporting detection of changes in the underlying interpretation of the input data by the model, monitoring the concept rather than the data, while matching established drift detection methods metrics-wise.

title: Fraud-Resilient Banking Through Hybrid Artificial Intelligence and Zero-Knowledge Proofs
abstract: Detecting fraud in digital banking is a recognized challenge given the increasing sophistication of perpetrators as well as the limitations of traditional security models. Rules-based systems produce interpretability but cannot be adapted to emerging fraud threats. Advanced machine learning models require complex systems for training and serving, which are often not practical in lightweight and real-time environments. In this work, a Java-based Hybrid Framework for Fraud-Resilient Banking Systems is built that combines rule-based compliance, lightweight AI modeling, anomaly detection, and the application of cryptographic concept of Zero Knowledge Proof (ZKP) authentication in a decision layer. A synthetic dataset of 10,000 banking transactions representing realistic imbalances has been developed, with approximately 0.6% flagging transactions as fraudulent. The rules for interpretable transparency are applied in the event of high-value transactions or merchant transactions that are shown to be suspicious, the fraud detection is tackled through a logistic regression classifier to apply a probabilistic approach to fraud detection and z-scores have been used to identify anomalous outliers from an expected normal distribution as fraud. The framework included Schnorr’s ZKP protocol to authenticate the user without disclosing the secret credential. The consolidated scoring system incorporates the outputs of rules, AI probabilities, anomalies, and ZKP verification for sorting transactions into High, Medium, and Low risk. The experimental results on the Java implementation shows an achievable ROC AUC of 0.984. The system produces a balanced risk distribution, for 1.8% of transactions classified as high risk, 20% medium risk and 78% low risk. This research suggests that a lightweight Java-based fraud detection system can be made efficient, interpretable, and cryptographically augmented, and thus usable in practice for a banking platform where performance and security are key.

title: AI-Driven Virtual Assistant with Immersive Experience
abstract: Intelligent Virtual Assistants (IVAs) are advancing with multimodal AI, yet existing systems still struggle with contextual reasoning, emotion awareness, and natural interaction inside immersive environments. This research presents a hybrid IVA framework that integrates speech recognition, emotion analysis, and generative reasoning with a photorealistic 3D avatar for real-time XR interaction. The system combines Azure Cognitive Services for intent classification with a domain-adapted Mistral LLM for deeper contextual understanding, supported by a lightweight vision module for facial emotion detection. A viseme-synchronized avatar rendering pipeline produces lifelike conversational behavior, enabling seamless multimodal interaction through speech, gaze, and expressionsExperimental evaluation shows that the hybrid model improves intent accuracy, response coherence, and user engagement compared to traditional IVA architectures. The results demonstrate that integrating cognitive AI with immersive avatar-based visualization enhances realism and usability in training, technical support, and interactive assistance scenarios. This work provides a scalable foundation for next-generation, emotion-aware virtual assistants capable of delivering more human-like and context-adaptive interactions in XR environments.

title: Evaluating Generative AI’s Role in Enhancing Hotel Guests’ Purchase Intentions
abstract: This study investigates how guests form perceptions about using generative AI systems when seeking recommendations for local attractions and how these perceptions influence their subsequent purchase intentions. A conceptual model was constructed based on Social Exchange Theory and empirically validated using data from an online survey of 398 U.S. guests. The findings reveal that perceived benefit and trust in AI have a moderately significant effect on intentions to purchase, while reciprocity has a minor significant impact. Additionally, uncertainty avoidance has a minor significant negative effect on intentions to purchase. At a time when monetizing consumers’ use of technology is increasingly critical, this study explains purchase intentions driven by hotels’ use of generative AI, which is instrumental in advancing research on the impact of generative AI.

title: PWACG: Partial wave analysis code generator supporting Newton-conjugate gradient method
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Partial Wave Analysis Code Generator (PWACG) that automatically generates high-performance partial wave analysis codes. This is achieved by leveraging the JAX automatic differentiation library and the jinja2 template engine. The resulting code is constructed using the high-performance API of JAX, and includes support for the Newton’s Conjugate Gradient optimization method, as well as the full utilization of parallel computing capabilities offered by GPUs. By harnessing these advanced computing techniques, PWACG demonstrates a significant advantage in efficiently identifying global optimal points compared to conventional partial wave analysis software packages.

title: Image Segmentation Used Different Machine and Deep Learning Technology for Breast Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: This study will examine MetaAI's 2023 Segment Anything Model (SAM) and apply it to medical image segmentation. Second, this study compares SAM's medical picture segmentation to other models. Mass and calcification mammograms in the diverse Curated Breast Imaging Subset of the DDSM (CBIS-DDSM) dataset acknowledge breast cancer's diversity and expose segmentation methods to different scenarios, making the research strong. This study compares medical picture segmentation using prompt-based models (SAM) and EncoderDecoder architectures (UNet,UNet++, Attention-UNet, SegNet). This study evaluates models using dice score, IoU, and accuracy. This breakthrough enhances breast cancer diagnosis by increasing medical image segmentation. ML and DL methods for breast cancer detection and risk assessment are extensively investigated in this paper. This research analyses the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Database (WBCD) and NKI Breast Cancer dataset using machine and deep learning. In the study, data preparation, feature selection, and 10-fold cross-validation increase model performance. CNN accuracy on WBCD was 96.12% while Decision Tree accuracy on NKI was 89%. Precision and recall measure model performance. This holistic study addresses previous research limitations and emphasizes the usefulness of diverse datasets in breast cancer diagnosis accuracy, which may improve healthcare.

title: Autonomous Agents and Policy Compliance: A Framework for Reasoning About Penalties
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a logic programming-based framework for policy-aware autonomous agents that can reason about potential penalties for noncompliance and act accordingly. While prior work has primarily focused on ensuring compliance, our approach considers scenarios where deviating from policies may be necessary to achieve high-stakes goals. Additionally, modeling noncompliant behavior can assist policymakers by simulating realistic human decision-making. Our framework extends Gelfond and Lobo’s Authorization and Obligation Policy Language ( $\mathscr{AOPL}$ ) to incorporate penalties and integrates Answer Set Programming (ASP) for reasoning. Compared to previous approaches, our method ensures well-formed policies, accounts for policy priorities, and enhances explainability by explicitly identifying rule violations and their consequences. Building on the work of Harders and Inclezan, we introduce penalty-based reasoning to distinguish between noncompliant plans, prioritizing those with minimal repercussions. To support this, we develop an automated translation from the extended $\mathscr{AOPL}$ into ASP and refine ASP-based planning algorithms to account for incurred penalties. Experiments in two domains demonstrate that our framework generates higher-quality plans that avoid harmful actions while, in some cases, also improving computational efficiency. These findings underscore its potential for enhancing autonomous decision-making and informing policy refinement.

title: An Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis Dataset of Skincare Product Reviews from Bangladeshi E-Commerce Platforms
abstract: This dataset presents an aspect-level sentiment annotated corpus of skincare product reviews collected from major Bangladeshi e-commerce platforms (Shajgoj, Ogerio, and Ohsogo). It comprises 2,003 aspect-level annotated instances, developed to support Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) in the skincare domain. The dataset captures fine-grained consumer opinions by associating specific product aspects with corresponding sentiment polarity. The data is structured into the following fields: Product Name: Name of the skincare product Product Category: Category of the product (e.g., Sunscreen) Rating: User-provided rating on a 1–5 scale Review Date: Date when the review was posted Review Text: Customer-written review content Aspect-Sentiment Annotation: Aspect category paired with sentiment polarity in JSON format The dataset covers seven aspect categories—Suitability, Effectiveness, Quality, Texture, Sensitivity, Satisfaction, and Others—with sentiment labels classified as Positive or Negative. Reviews containing multiple aspects are split into separate aspect-level entries. The corpus was curated from real user reviews and manually annotated to ensure consistency and labeling accuracy. Applications: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis Opinion Mining Text Classification Consumer Behavior Analysis Explainable AI in E-commerce

title: Exploring the Synergy of Quantum-Classical Integration in Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms have gained attention as a promising strategy to harness the advantages of both quantum and classical computing for machine learning applications. This review delves into the potential of these algorithms to address the limitations inherent in purely classical or quantum methods, offering a thorough overview of the current landscape in this area. We cover the basics of quantum computing, such as qubits, superposition, and entanglement, and emphasize the challenges that both quantum and classical computing face in the realm of machine learning. Various hybrid frameworks, including quantum-classical neural networks, quantum-enhanced optimization algorithms, and quantum feature maps, are explored in depth. We examine specific hybrid algorithms, like the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), assessing their potential to enhance data preprocessing, feature selection, model training, and inference. The role of quantum-inspired algorithms in bridging the gap between quantum and classical methods is also discussed. We investigate the scalability of hybrid approaches and their potential to capitalize on future advancements in quantum hardware, while considering implementation challenges such as quantum error correction and noise mitigation. The implications of these algorithms for privacy, security, fairness, and interpretability in machine learning are analyzed. Finally, we consider the potential impact of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms on various industries and their integration with other emerging technologies. This review offers a comprehensive perspective on the current state and future directions of this rapidly evolving field.

title: Symmetric Encryption and XOR-Based Model for E-Commerce Ecosystem
abstract: One of the most common activities computer users perform is exchanging information or data, particularly through e-commerce platforms. The transferred data is often sensitive and must be protected from unauthorized access. A specialized scientific field known as cryptography has emerged in response to this need. Cryptography focuses on securing data by converting it from a readable format (plaintext) into an unreadable format (ciphertext), using specific keys and algorithms to prevent unauthorized interpretation. A cryptographic key and an appropriate encryption algorithm are required to secure data with a password. As encryption technologies evolve, encryption keys have become more accessible through various methods. Consequently, many cryptographic algorithms have been developed to ensure data security. One such method is the substitution cipher, a classical encryption technique. However, ciphertext can be analyzed using cryptanalysis to uncover the original encryption key, which can then be used to decrypt the ciphertext back into plaintext. Cryptanalysis techniques often begin by identifying the key length and then deducing the correct key combination to access the encrypted information. In this study, the author investigates the cryptanalytic process applied to the substitution cipher algorithm using two paired key models: the Symmetric and XOR-based models. The aim is to evaluate the complexity and security of these approaches in safeguarding data and transactions within the e-commerce environment. Objective: To examine the mechanism of electronic transactions (e-commerce) through internet-based payment systems with a focus on security, and to evaluate how these transactions comply with the Information Technology (IT) Act regarding the protection of consumer information.

title: Adaptive Temporal Neural Networks for Individualized Diabetes Risk Prediction from Irregular Health Records
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder that afflicts millions of individuals globally, and throughout most cases the disease remains asymptomatic prior to diagnosis. Early identification of high risk individuals can greatly improve clinical outcome and reduce health care costs. Nevertheless, between these two points, electronic health records (EHRs)—a rich and central data source for predictive modeling—tend to be temporally-irregular, sparse, and person-specific, rendering risk prediction difficult. In this paper, we introduce an Adaptive Temporal Neural Network (ATNN) approach to individualized diabetes risk prediction from non-uniform EHR data. Unlike traditional methods that rely on constant sampling intervals, ATNN adapts to the input time gap and sequence pattern variations in a dynamic way with a hybrid input mechanism involving Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and temporal attentions. It also integrates demographic and lifestyle information in an add-on to personalize risk trajectories across time. We test our model on a large-scale EHR dataset with over 20000 patients and compare it with a series of baselines including logistic regression, RNNs and Transformer-based models. Experiments demonstrate that ATNN outperforms state-of-the-art models in the presence of missing data, irregularly sampled time series and inter-individual model variance, yielding an AUC of 0.91. This research results emphasize the significance of temporal adaptation and individualized variations in prediction of chronic disease and reveal the power of neural temporal modeling for predictive medicine.

title: ANALISIS REPRESENTASI CHATBOT DALAM MEDIA SOSIAL, HIBURAN, DAN DAMPAKNYA TERHADAP BUDAYA DIGITAL
abstract: The development of chatbots today has shaped new ways for humans to interact in an all-digital environment. Chatbots are no longer understood as tools that simply answer simple questions, but have evolved into entities that are present and play a role in various digital spaces, from education, mental health, social media, entertainment, to pop culture communities. This study presents an overview to understand how chatbots are represented, used, and interpreted in digital culture. The findings indicate that chatbots increasingly play a role in emotional and social aspects, and make important contributions to shaping people's digital experiences. Various studies highlight how chatbots can support the learning process, facilitate information navigation, and provide emotional support for their users. Overall, these findings confirm that chatbots have become a significant element in modern digital life and open new spaces for discussions about ethics, the need for more context-sensitive design, and the development of technology that centers the human experience.

title: Schmidt Concentration as Lock-In Amplifier for Classical Phase Verification in Monitored Quantum Circuits
abstract: Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices require efficient diagnostics for verifying state preparation and quantum Zeno dynamics. Conventional approaches using von Neumann entropy S_vN exhibit divergent variance in the measurement-dominated classical phase, precisely where verification is most critical. We demonstrate that the Schmidt concentration index κ = Σλᵢ² provides phase-dependent complementary information with superior stability in the classical regime. Through numerical simulations of Haar-random circuits with projective measurements (L=12 qubits, 100 trajectories per measurement rate), we find that while κ exhibits higher variance than S_vN in the quantum phase (coefficient of variation ratio CV(κ)/CV(S) = 5.1), it achieves 4-fold lower variance in the classical phase (CV(κ)/CV(S) = 0.25). This crossover occurs at measurement rate p ≈ 0.27, establishing κ as a lock-in amplifier for classical phase characterization. The enhanced stability translates to a 75% reduction in required measurement shots for equivalent verification confidence, offering immediate practical value for NISQ state preparation protocols and error correction threshold detection.

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN TERHADAP MAKAN BERGIZI GRATIS PADA SOSIAL MEDIA X MENGGUNAKAN METODE DECICION TREE DENGAN PEMBANDING NAIVE BAYES
abstract: Media sosial X (sebelumnya Twitter) telah menjadi tempat yang populer bagi orang-orang untuk berbagi pendapat, termasuk tentang program sosial seperti makan bergizi gratis yang belakangan ini menjadi perhatian publik. Tujuan dari program ini adalah untuk meningkatkan kesehatan masyarakat, terkhusus bagi anak-anak sekolah. Program ini menerima banyak tanggapan dari masyarakat, yang sebagian besar positif. Dengan menggunakan teknik klasifikasi Decision Tree, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk melihat bagaimana orang-orang di media sosial X melihat program makan bergizi gratis. Data dikumpulkan melalui proses crawling dengan kata kunci "Makan Bergizi Gratis", lalu dilakukan perbaikan, tokenisasi, penghapusan kata kunci, dan stemming. Setelah algoritma Decision Tree digunakan untuk melakukan klasifikasi, hasil evaluasi digunakan untuk membandingkannya dengan algoritma Naïve Bayes. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa algoritma Decision Tree memiliki akurasi sebesar 76,38%, dengan kinerja yang baik terutama pada kelas sentimen positif. Sementara itu, algoritma Naïve Bayes memiliki akurasi sebesar 75,59%, tetapi distribusi prediksinya cenderung tidak merata di antara kelas sentimen. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa metode Decision Tree mampu memberikan klasifikasi yang cukup seimbang untuk menangani data sentimen multi-kelas dan memberikan gambaran umum tentang persepsi publik terhadap kebijakan makan bergizi gratis di Indonesia

title: Advancing Bengali Next-Word Prediction: A Multi-Domain Text Dataset for Language Modelling and Predictive Text
abstract: This is a comprehensive collection of Bengali texts drawn from multiple areas of discourse to support research into Bengali language modeling and next-word prediction. The data was compiled in Summer 2025 from 32 publically available sources which contain a wide variety of writing styles and topics (i.e., national news portals; Wikipedia; Class IX-X textbooks; religious and ethical writings; literature and poetry; blogs; publicly visible social media text; and a small number of clearly labeled examples generated by an artificial intelligence). All data was stored in UTF-8 Bengali Unicode text format and grouped at the source level to enable transparent provenance tracking, domain-based testing, and experimental replication. With respect to size, this combined corpus contained 503,257 tokens and 84,788 unique word forms before preprocessing and 498,023 tokens and 62,009 unique word forms after preprocessing, providing a large body of data for training, benchmarking, and comparative analysis of both statistical and neural methods for Bengali next-word prediction.

title: An Explainable AI Framework for Interpretable Cybercrime Detection Using Multi-Source Digital Evidence
abstract: While modern cybersecurity systems rely on machine learning models with high predictive accuracy, operational deployment also demands interpretable decision-making to help security analysts understand the rationale behind alerts—particularly when evidence originates from heterogeneous sources such as network flows, URLs, and email text. This paper presents an Explainable AI (XAI) framework for transparent cybercrime detection using diverse multi-source datasets, including CIC-IDS2017, CIC-Phishing 2019, and the Malicious URL 2020 corpus. Representative positive and negative samples are extracted from each dataset, and a unified preprocessing pipeline is applied for normalization, vectorization, and consolidation of raw features before training ensemble and deep learning classifiers. To address black-box limitations, the framework integrates SHAP for global feature attribution, LIME for local instance-level explanation, and attention-based visualization for sequence-oriented inputs. Experimental results demonstrate that XGBoost and a BiLSTM–Attention model achieve the highest detection performance, with accuracies of 94.8% and 95.6%, respectively. XAI analysis further reveals that network flow statistics, lexical URL characteristics, and email header anomalies are the most influential predictors across modalities. These findings confirm that XAI techniques enhance model transparency and trustworthiness without compromising predictive performance. The proposed interpretable detection framework enables actionable insight for analysts and lays the foundation for future multimodal, real-world explainable cyber-defense systems.

title: Multi-dimensional Safety Verification System for AI: Dynamic Robustness and Antifragility Assessment through Interferometric Stress Testing
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic AI safety verification framework that goes beyond static datasets and conventional simulations. By treating safety testing as an interferometric process, it generates synthetic threat vectors whose constructive interference amplifies hidden vulnerabilities that remain undetected in isolated tests. The framework evaluates dynamic robustness as phase cancellation against disturbances and introduces an Antifragility metric, measuring the AI’s ability to improve under socio-economic stress. This approach establishes a new safety standard focused on adaptive, self-correcting resilience for AI deployed in social infrastructure.

title: Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Aplikasi Mobile Banking BCA Mobile dan Brimo Menggunakan Metode Naive Bayes
abstract: The rapid development of digital financial technology in Indonesia has led to increased use of mobile banking applications as the primary medium for customer transactions. Two widely used platforms are BCA Mobile and BRImo, both of which receive various user reviews on the Google Play Store. This study aims to analyze user sentiment toward these applications using the Multinomial Naïve Bayes method and TF–IDF feature weighting. The dataset consists of 18,034 reviews that have undergone text preprocessing, including cleansing, case folding, tokenizing, normalization, filtering, and stemming, as well as lexicon-based sentiment labeling into two classes: positive and negative. The evaluation results show that the developed model achieves an accuracy of 96% for BRImo and 91% for BCA Mobile, demonstrating strong performance in identifying and distinguishing positive and negative reviews. Overall, reviews for BRImo are predominantly positive, while BCA Mobile also shows a positive tendency but receives a higher number of complaints. These findings are expected to provide useful insights for mobile banking developers in improving service quality and enhancing user experience.

title: FedPML: Federated Prototype Meta-Learning for Adaptation and Generalization in Distributed Environments
abstract: Federated learning (FL) holds significant promise for enabling automatic modulation classification (AMC) across distributed wireless Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems while preserving data privacy. Yet, its deployment in real-world scenarios is hindered by two fundamental limitations: the inability to generalize across non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) clients without sacrificing personalization, and the lack of fast, data-efficient local adaptation mechanisms under non-IID, resource-constrained conditions. In this work, we present FedPML, a novel federated prototype-based meta-learning framework that directly addresses these challenges through a unified and scalable approach. FedPML leverages a lightweight Reptile-based meta-optimization strategy and class-level prototypes to jointly optimize for cross-client consistency and local task adaptability. This design enables rapid personalization with minimal data and computation, while preserving global knowledge alignment across heterogeneous clients. Extensive experiments on standard AMC benchmarks under a wide range of IID and non-IID conditions show that FedPML consistently outperforms strong FL baselines, achieving higher accuracy, faster convergence, and reduced communication overhead. The results demonstrate that FedPML is a powerful and practical solution for realizing resilient, low-latency AMC in decentralized IoT networks.

title: Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning for Multi-Tenant CRM Workflows: Integrating Homomorphic Encryption across Cloud Databases
abstract: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platforms increasingly integrate deep learning models to support predictive analytics, personalization, and automated decision-making. In cloud-based, multi-tenant environments, these capabilities introduce significant privacy risks, as sensitive customer data from multiple tenants is processed on shared infrastructure. Conventional security mechanisms, such as encryption at rest and in transit, fail to protect data during model training and inference, where exposure risks are highest. Homomorphic encryption offers a promising approach by enabling computation directly on encrypted data, preserving confidentiality throughout the analytics lifecycle. However, integrating homomorphic encryption into deep learning workflows presents substantial challenges related to system architecture, performance overhead, and operational complexity. This paper examines privacy-preserving deep learning for multi-tenant CRM workflows through the lens of practical enterprise deployment. It analyzes architectural patterns for integrating homomorphic encryption across cloud databases, explores workflow-level design considerations, and evaluates trade-offs between privacy guarantees and system efficiency. By focusing on real-world CRM pipelines rather than purely cryptographic abstractions, the study provides actionable guidance for designing scalable, compliant, and privacy-aware deep learning systems in modern cloud environments.

title: Supplementary Material for "A Comparative Evaluation of Privacy-Preserving Data Publication Techniques"
abstract: This repository contains the code, detailed privacy–utility results, and analysis notebooks used in the comparative evaluation of privacy-preserving data publication techniques. Top-level directories and files data/ Raw and intermediate data files used for privacy and utility analysis. figures/ Generated figures used in the paper (e.g., heatmaps, trade-off plots, correlation matrices). helper.py Shared utility functions used across analysis notebooks (e.g., data loading, preprocessing, metric computation, plotting helpers). privacy_gain_analysis.ipynb Analysis notebook for computing and aggregating privacy gain metrics across datasets, scenarios, and settings (QID vs. all columns). privacy_metrics_correlation_analysis.ipynb Notebook for analysing correlations among privacy metrics and between privacy and utility metrics. privacy_utility_trade_off_analysis.ipynb Notebook for studying privacy–utility trade-offs using cross-correlation matrices and visualisations. utility_loss_analysis.ipynb Analysis of downstream utility loss, including ML efficacy, optimisation utility (RAU), and count query error (CQE). README.md Documentation describing the project structure, experimental setup, and how to reproduce the results. source-code/ Contains scripts, datasets, and configuration files related to data processing and experiment execution. Datasets/ Original datasets used in the experiments. It contains the ACSIncome dataset. We, however, do exclude the patient data set from this publication, as it was retracted at the request of the data subject or controller. Hierarchies/ Attribute generalisation hierarchies used for de-identification (e.g., QID generalisation). We used the same hierarchies to calculate categorical distances for both datasets. output/ Generated outputs from experiments, including intermediate results and processed datasets. intellij/ The IntelliJ folder contains an IntelliJ project that implements de-identification using the ARX anonymisation library. From this code, a .jar file is generated, used to produce de-identified datasets. pycharm/ The PyCharm folder contains all the Python code needed to reproduce the results. This folder is structured as follows: dataset_preparation: contains code to obtain the ACSIncome dataset and preprocess both the ACSIncome and Patients datasets (results in ACSIncome.csv and Patients_cleaned.csv) privacy: contains the privacy metric implementations and additional helper functions to perform the metric calculations utility: contains the use-case-specific and statistical utility metric implementations DistanceMetrics: contains the custom distance calculations pipeline: contains code to run all experiments in order results_condenser: contains code to merge the obtained results into a limited set of files

title: A Cloud-Agnostic Machine Learning Framework for Mass-Level Early Breast Cancer Detection and Risk Prediction in Rural India
abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality among women globally, with disproportionately high late-stage detection rates in low-resource rural settings. This paper addresses the critical need for accessible, low-cost screening infrastructure in rural areas of Bihar, India, where geographical, economic, and socio-cultural barriers (including significant stigma) impede timely diagnosis. We propose a robust, two-tiered Machine Learning (ML) framework designed for Edge Computing deployment. The framework utilizes two models: 1) A Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), fine-tuned using Transfer Learning on the public CBIS-DDSM dataset, for the binary classification of suspicious lesions identified in imaging/scanning data. 2) A Random Forest Classifier trained on structured clinical and demographic data to provide personalized, localized breast cancer risk prediction.

title: Weakly supervised deep multi-instance learning for classification of endometrial lesions on hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images
abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecological malignancy, yet reliable screening and diagnostic approaches remain limited. We developed a weakly supervised deep multi-instance learning model (DSMIL) to classify hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) of endometrial tissue. A total of 885 WSIs from 442 patients, including EC, atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH), endometrial hyperplasia without atypia (EH), and normal endometrium (NE), were analyzed. DSMIL achieved an average AUROC of 0.9776 for four-class classification, with inter-class AUROCs of 0.9876 for EC, 0.9600 for AEH, 0.9771 for EH, and 0.9855 for NE, and outperformed other algorithms such as TransMSL, CLAM, and ABMIL (average accuracy = 0.8914). Attention heatmaps highlighted regions associated with pathological features, while nnU-Net v2 combined with HoverNet enabled identification of atypical glandular epithelial cells, which showed increased density, size, and perimeter but reduced axis ratios compared with normal cells. These results suggest that DSMIL provides a reliable computational pathology approach for the classification of endometrial lesions and the characterization of atypical cells.

title: Auditable Drag and Drop AI Pipelines: OCR LLM Composition with Rubric Scoring, HITL, and Provenance First MLOps
abstract: We present an auditable, drag-and-drop platform for composing OCR–LLM pipelines with explainability, rubric-based scoring, human-in-the-loop (HITL) review, and provenance-first MLOps. Blocks encapsulate OCR detectors/recognizers, promp table LLM extractors, XAI widgets, scoring policies, and review queues. A Node-RED-style orchestrator records configuration, model/version, inputs/outputs, and human actions to a relational store for replay and audit. We formalize rubric scoring as a constrained, weighted objective and pair it with explanations (Grad-CAM/Score-CAM overlays, token-level rationales) to justify decisions. HITL patterns (escalation, adjudication, exception) close the loop for reliability and compliance. On ICDAR SROIE (receipts) and FUNSD (forms) we report OCR/KIE F1, end-to-end latency, reviewer time per operation, and provenance coverage. Results show competitive accuracy with traceable decision trails, offering a practical template for trustworthy, policy-constrained document AI in production.

evidence.abstract: We present an auditable, drag-and-drop platform for composing OCR–LLM pipelines with explainability, rubric-based scoring, human-in-the-loop (HITL) review, and provenance-first MLOps. Blocks encapsulate OCR detectors/recognizers, promp table LLM extractors, XAI widgets, scoring policies, and review queues. A Node-RED-style orchestrator records configuration, model/version, inputs/outputs, and human actions to a relational store for replay and audit. We formalize rubric scoring as a constrained, weighted objective and pair it with explanations (Grad-CAM/Score-CAM overlays, token-level rationales) to justify decisions. HITL patterns (escalation, adjudication, exception) close the loop for reliability and compliance. On ICDAR SROIE (receipts) and FUNSD (forms) we report OCR/KIE F1, end-to-end latency, reviewer time per operation, and provenance coverage. Results show competitive accuracy with traceable decision trails, offering a practical template for trustworthy, policy-constrained document AI in production.

title: AI-driven adaptive stealth assessment for socially regulated learning in collaborative environments
abstract: Conventional digital assessments often overlook learners’ real-time progress, peer interactions, and cognitive demands. This study addresses these limitations by introducing GenSolve, an adaptive artificial intelligence (AI)-driven stealth assessment framework designed to adjust scenario complexity, deliver personalized feedback, and monitor group regulation using socially regulated learning (SoRL) principles. A six-week quasi-experimental study involving 250 undergraduates compared GenSolve to traditional instruction. Results showed a 17.6% gain in problem-solving accuracy, a 21% increase in group cohesion, and a 12.7% improvement in delayed retention. AI-generated feedback reduced repeated errors by 23.4% and improved self-regulation, while SoRL mechanisms supported a 36% rise in independent conflict resolution. GenSolve contributes a scalable, ethically guided model for real-time collaborative assessment, offering practical advances in adaptive evaluation for digital learning environments.

title: ECDLP Quantum Cryptanalysis
abstract: We demonstrate genuine quantum cryptanalysis of the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem up to 14 bits on IBM's 156-qubit Heron R2 processor. Unlike planted-key demonstrations, our implementation uses a full group operation oracle that recovers private keys without prior knowledge. We establish that algorithm structure dictates optimal transpilation: SABRE achieves 47% gate reduction over HOT for QFT-dominated circuits. Our key finding reframes success metrics—at 14 bits, the correct key ranked #535 among 1,806 candidates, yet provided 9.1× keyspace reduction. All results are independently verifiable via IBM Quantum Platform job artifacts.

title: Autonomous Reality Convergence System Based on Resonant Computation and Federated Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes an autonomous reality convergence system that integrates resonant computation, federated artificial intelligence, and controlled physical intervention. By abandoning sequential computation in favor of resonance, the system eliminates computational latency. A federation of specialized AI models enables unlimited scalability without performance saturation, while blueprint-based, safeguarded interventions allow AI to actively and safely influence reality. Incorporating antifragile design, circuit breakers, and a meta-ethical feedback layer, the architecture transforms AI from a passive analytical tool into a stable, socially aligned agent capable of guiding reality toward evolving ideal states.

title: A Tuning-Free Constrained Team-Oriented Swarm Optimizer (CTOSO) for Engineering Problems
abstract: Constrained optimization problems (COPs) are frequent in engineering design yet remain challenging due to complex search spaces and strict feasibility requirements. Existing swarm-based optimizers often rely on penalty functions or algorithm-specific control parameters, whose performance is sensitive to problem-dependent tuning and may lead to premature convergence or infeasible solutions when feasible regions are narrow. This paper introduces the Constrained Team-Oriented Swarm Optimizer (CTOSO), a tuning-free metaheuristic that adapts the ETOSO framework by replacing linear exploiter movement with spiral search and integrating Deb’s feasibility rule. The population divides into Explorers, promoting diversity through neighbor-guided navigation, and Exploiters, performing intensified local search around the global best solution. Extensive evaluation on twelve constrained engineering benchmark problems shows that CTOSO achieves a 100% feasibility rate and attains the highest overall composite performance score among the compared algorithms under limited function-evaluation budgets. On the CEC 2017 constrained benchmark suite, CTOSO attains an average feasibility rate of 79.78%, generating feasible solutions on 14 out of 15 problems. Statistical analysis using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Friedman ranking with Nemenyi post hoc comparison indicates that CTOSO performs significantly better than several baseline optimizers, while exhibiting no statistically significant differences with leading evolutionary methods under the same experimental conditions. The algorithm’s design, requiring no tuning of algorithm-specific control parameters, makes it suitable for real-world engineering applications where tuning effort must be minimized.

title: Design Hybrid System for Secure Cloud Storage based on Advanced Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Cloud computing has innovated data processing and storage with its scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. Classic encryption methods guarantee the confidentiality of data, but these methods necessitate decryption for processing, thus revealing the data to possible breaches. The SecCloud-HHE (Secure Cloud Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption) is the subject of this paper, and it is a hybrid encryption architecture designed for secure and efficient cloud data storage. The combination of homomorphic encryption for encrypted computation and attribute-based encryption for fine-grained access control gives SecCloud-HHE confidentiality, scalability and controlled access. The encryption and decryption times for the smallest files (24 bytes) were very low and measured at 4.13 ms and 0.90 ms, respectively. The timings for the biggest files (8248 bytes) were still 1319.34 ms for encryption and 311.21 ms for decryption, which are very long but still practical, thus showing the algorithm's scalability. Cipher text representing a linear growth, rising from fragments of 28 bits to 8270 bits, assures the stable overweightness of storage. The time for key generation and verification also increased linearly. When compared to the current methods such as ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography), KP-ABE (Key-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption), and VFHE-DWOA (Verifiable Fully Homomorphic Encryption with Dynamic Weighted Optimization Algorithm), SecCloud-HHE lagged behind all with no noticeable delay. The findings back the framework's appropriateness for live and limited-resource cloud settings, thus providing a safe, effective, and scalable option for encrypted data processing, as well as for access control.

title: Rex to the rescue: Evaluating the effectiveness of real-time AI-driven stealth assessment and support for mathematical modeling in virtual science investigations
abstract: Stealth assessment, rooted in evidence-centered design (ECD), provides an unobtrusive means of assessing students’ competencies in online environments. This paper presents a formative, performance-based assessment in the Inquiry Intelligent Tutoring System (Inq-ITS), designed using ECD and integrating AI-driven stealth assessment to provide targeted, real-time support for students’ mathematical modeling in science investigations. We examined the effectiveness of the targeted support from an AI-based pedagogical agent, Rex, in ninth-grade physical science classrooms. Results showed that students with lower math proficiency had significant learning gains when Rex was available, compared to similar students without Rex. These findings highlight the power of stealth assessment to provide real-time data and support, while offering empirical evidence of how students are learning essential science and math competencies aligned to the NGSS.

title: A Review on Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Architectures, Research Challenges, and Emerging Frontiers
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge retrieval into the generation pipeline, enabling responses that are grounded, adaptive, and up to date. While RAG can improve factual accuracy compared to models relying solely on pre-trained data, its effectiveness in practice depends strongly on the quality, relevance, and interpretability of retrieved context, and does not eliminate hallucinations entirely. Recent architectures such as Fusion-in-Decoder, Atlas, and ColBERT-RAG demonstrate measurable gains in retrieval precision, scalability, and cross-domain generalization. However, persistent challenges remain, including retrieval noise that can override model reasoning, hallucinations that persist even with high-quality evidence, latency constraints that hinder real-time deployment, and fragile domain adaptation. Moreover, although partial metrics and task-specific benchmarks exist, the absence of a unified evaluation framework for retrieval–generation grounding and robustness complicates fair comparison and reproducible progress. Rather than offering an exhaustive survey, this review provides a focused analytical perspective on retrieval design and architectural evolution in RAG systems. It consolidates representative architectures while critically examining structural limitations related to retrieval–generation coupling as a design choice, context over-reliance, and privacy-preserving computation. Building on these insights, the paper outlines future research directions, including structured knowledge integration via GraphRAG, modular agent-based orchestration in Agentic RAG, improved retrieval filtering, and unified evaluation methodologies. As RAG architectures continue to evolve rapidly in a pre-standardization phase, a more analytically grounded understanding of their design trade-offs is essential for advancing trustworthy and domain-adaptive language systems

title: Artificial Intelligence Awareness Among School Students
abstract: Based on existing research methods, this paper depends on the concept of artificial intelligence and its impact on society and various fields, health industry, education sector etc. The research is done by qualitative and quantitative analysis of the data and statistics in turn which results in how Artificial Intelligence has become a fast growing name in technology. In this survey we found out that many Individuals are aware of that they are encountering artificial intelligence (AI) in daily life, such as Robotic Mop, Movie recommendations, customer service chatbots and product recommendations based on previous purchases etc. Simultaneously, only three-in-ten adults are able to correctly identify all ten uses of AI asked about in the survey, underscoring the developing nature of public understanding.

title: AGENTIC COLLAPSE: A Time-Delayed Cybernetic Framework for Epistemic Stability in Autonomous AI Systems
abstract: The transition from static Large Language Models to dynamic Autonomous Agents has introduced a new class of epistemic failure modes driven by the “Orchestration Penalty”—the factorial increase in verification complexity inherent to multi-step reasoning loops. This research identifies a structural “Latency Killer” in System 2 architectures, where the velocity of agentic action ($\phi$) inherently outpaces the latency of deliberate verification ($\tau_{sys2}$). We introduce a time-delayed stochastic dynamical system ($d\phi, d\psi, dU$) that models the accumulation of “Agentic Drift.” Simulation results reveal a catastrophic phase transition termed “Agentic Collapse,” where a stochastic complexity spike ($t \approx 60$) drives the system into an irretrievable high-entropy state before the lagged verifier can compensate. We demonstrate that perfect stability is mathematically impossible in open-ended agentic loops; instead, safety requires a regime of “Metastability” enforced by a “Popperian Guillotine”—a discrete safety interlock that resets the agent when epistemic potential exceeds a critical threshold ($U_{crit}=0.88$). Finally, we derive an “Epistemic Speed Limit,” arguing that robust autonomy requires dynamically throttling execution speed to match the “Cost of Thought.”

title: PERANCANGAN GAME 2D TOP-DOWN SHOOTER "OUTBREAK25" MENGGUNAKAN METODE FINITE STATE MACHINE (FSM) DAN PROCEDURAL GENERATION
abstract: Game merupakan hiburan digital yang berkembang pesat, namun banyak game masih menggunakan level statis dan musuh dengan perilaku sederhana sehingga cepat membosankan. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengembangkan Outbreak25, game 2D top-down shooter berbasis desktop yang menggabungkan kecerdasan buatan dan generasi level otomatis. Metode yang digunakan mencakup Finite State Machine (FSM) untuk mengatur perilaku musuh seperti patroli, pengejaran, dan serangan, serta Procedural Generation untuk membentuk peta permainan dinamis. Game dikembangkan menggunakan Unity Engine dan diuji melalui pengujian Black Box, FSM, Procedural Generation, kontrol pemain, kompatibilitas perangkat, dan tanggapan pengguna. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan seluruh fitur berjalan sesuai fungsinya: FSM dan procedural generation berjalan adaptif, kontrol responsif, dan game kompatibel di berbagai perangkat. Pada uji pengguna terhadap 13 responden, 70,51% responden memilih "Iya", sedangkan 29,48% responden memilih "Tidak". Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, Outbreak25 dinilai berhasil dari sisi teknis, fungsional, dan pengalaman pengguna, serta memiliki potensi pengembangan lebih lanjut.

title: Toward Robust Offensive Language Detection in Urdu YouTube Discourse
abstract: This study addresses the task of detecting offensive language in Urdu text on social media, where harmful and offensive comments can lead to emotional distress. Using a dataset of Urdu comments collected from YouTube news channels, both deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) models were employed for offensive language detection. Feature extraction was performed using Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and the Count Vectorizer approach to capture unigrams, bigrams, and trigrams. Four ML models—Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gaussian Naive Bayes (NB)—were evaluated, with SVM achieving comparatively stronger performance among the ML approaches. For the deep learning framework, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures were implemented using custom Word2Vec and FastText embeddings. The experimental results indicated that the CNN model outperformed the other evaluated approaches, suggesting its effectiveness for detecting offensive language in Urdu text. title: The Impact of Sense of Power on Consumer Click-Through Intention Under AI Personalized Recommendation
abstract: This study investigates how consumers' sense of power influences their click-through intentions in AI-driven personalized recommendation systems. While prior research has explored personalized marketings impact on consumer behavior, the role of perceived power remains understudied. Through scenario-based experiments, we find that a heightened sense of power enhances engagement with AI recommendations, with self-efficacy as a key mediator. However, this effect weakens when privacy concerns are high, highlighting privacy as a critical moderating factor. Specifically, empowered consumers are more likely to interact with AI recommendations, but only when privacy risks are minimal. These findings deepen our understanding of consumer-AI interactions, emphasizing the need to balance personalization, user empowerment, and privacy protection. By integrating power dynamics into AI marketing, this research offers theoretical contributions and practical insights for designing ethically responsible and effective recommendation systems.

title: IMPLEMENTASI METODE FINITE STATE MACHINE (FSM) PADA GAME ADVENTURE 3D “JAKA TINGKIR : PENDEKAR PAJANG”
abstract: Game berbasis budaya memiliki potensi besar sebagai media edukasi interaktif. title: FraudGraph-X: A Scalable Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network Framework for Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection
abstract: Real-time fraud detection in large-scale financial systems remains a critical challenge due to the dynamic, sparse, and imbalanced nature of transactional data. Traditional machine learning models and even some deep learning methods fail to generalize effectively across evolving fraud patterns, often trading off between scalability, precision, and latency. This paper presents FraudGraph-X, a novel Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework designed to detect financial fraud in real time. FraudGraph-X integrates two parallel branches: a GraphSAGE-based spatial branch that captures transaction relationships, and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) branch that models sequential behavior. These branches are fused using a custom attention mechanism that highlights discriminative temporal-spatial features. The model is trained using a hybrid loss function comprising binary cross-entropy, focal loss, and temporal smoothness loss to address severe class imbalance and ensure consistent predictions across time. Evaluated on the Elliptic Bitcoin Transaction dataset, FraudGraph-X achieves an accuracy of 96.72%, precision of 94.85%, recall of 92.63%, and F1-score of 93.73%, outperforming state-of-the-art models like GCN, TGAT, and XGBoost. Moreover, the model delivers a real-time inference latency of 28.3 ms and a throughput of 1250 transactions per second, making it suitable for deployment in streaming environments. The results confirm that combining graph structure with time-aware learning significantly enhances detection accuracy and responsiveness. FraudGraph-X represents a scalable and interpretable advancement in fraud analytics for modern financial systems.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence: an empirical investigation in the organic food market
abstract: Purpose As the interface between companies and consumers becomes increasingly driven by artificial intelligence (AI) rather than by humans, this study investigates how purchase intentions differ in response to organic information delivered by AI versus human agents. By examining psychological drivers behind this difference, the research provides actionable insights for optimizing AI implementation in the organic market. Design/methodology/approach Three experiments are conducted and 555 participants are recruited to explore relationships among recommendation agents, trust, anthropomorphism and purchase intentions. Data are collected by an online research platform and analyzed by ANOVA and PROCESS 213. Findings The results find that consumers exhibit significantly greater willingness to purchase organic foods when information is provided by AI (vs. Human) in both online and offline scenarios. Also, consistent with previous studies, trust significantly mediates the relationship between received information and organic food purchase intentions. However, the data indicate that trust in integrity rather than in competence or benevolence emerges as the dominant factor in this market. Furthermore, the findings show that highly anthropomorphized AI agents significantly reduce perceived reliability of promotional information, thereby lowering purchase intentions for organic foods. Originality/value As organic is a credence attribute, establishing effective recommendation systems is crucial for marketers. This study examines the mechanism by which AI agents enhance the organic food purchasing intentions and thereby, extending the understanding of trust and the scope of AI applications in the market while offering practical suggestions for promoting organic foods in the AI era.

title: Entropy-Induced Collapse in Learned Decision Policies under Partial Observability and Architectural Mitigation
abstract: ACM/VERSION, This paper studies a previously undercharacterized failure mode of learned decision policies operating under partial observability. While data-driven policies often demonstrate superior efficiency in low-noise environments, we show that their operational stability degrades non-linearly as observation uncertainty increases. Rather than exhibiting graceful performance decay, learned policies undergo a sharp collapse characterized by high-variance behavior, excessive action switching, and elevated risk exposure. We formalize this phenomenon as entropy-induced policy collapse and analyze it within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework. Using entropy-based indicators derived from policy outputs, we identify a narrow transition region in which multiple instability signals co-occur, revealing an information-theoretic boundary on reliable policy operation. Through extensive simulation experiments, we demonstrate that this collapse is consistent across multiple model classes and is not resolved by architectural complexity alone. To address this limitation, we propose a Hybrid Meta-Control (HMC) architecture that supervises learned policies with entropy-aware fallback mechanisms. The proposed approach dynamically arbitrates between learned and heuristic controllers based on real-time estimates of uncertainty and instability. Our results show that the HMC architecture reduces collapse frequency by over 90% while preserving most of the efficiency gains of learned policies. These findings suggest that robustness in autonomous decision systems is fundamentally an architectural property rather than a purely statistical one, with implications for the deployment of learned controllers in safety- and reliability-critical domains.
